title: Single-cell profiling and genetic regulation of alternative polyadenylation in the human brain.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the data availability statement from the article HTML. Listed Zenodo 20740673 (CC-BY-4.0): 12 per-cell-type 3'aQTL/eQTL summary-statistic files of 160 MB-3.99 GB each, plus Scripts.zip; none downloaded (over the 50 MB cap). Downloaded and opened from the authors' public Broad directory: All_cts.Merged.pASite_MeanPDUI.tsv (48,118 rows; 34,365 unique proximal sites; 10,867 genes; 23 chromosomes; mean PDUI per cell type for 6 cell types, Exc filled for 34,387 rows, Mic for 1,291; 36,642 rows filled in only one cell type), All_cts.gAPA.Merged.tsv (6,706 lead 3'aQTL rows, 2,946 genes, rsID/hg38 position/slope), the AD differential-APA table (5,680 rows), individual_metadata_deidentified.tsv (427 donors, 238 with AD, 425 of 427 with race code 1), and the per-donor PDUI matrices Exc.PDUI_from_Dapars.rds (34,387 sites x 368 donors, 0 missing) and Mic (1,291 x 284). All files parsed on the first try (tsv via pandas, rds via Rscript).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 2 million cells, 379 brains, 4,288 3'aQTL genes, 168 GWAS loci and pQTL colocalization come from the abstract. I did not read the methods, so the exact PDUI definition (I assume the DaPars distal-usage fraction, 0 to 1) and the filters are inferred from the file names and the field. Raw snRNA-seq (single-nucleus RNA sequencing) and genotypes are on Synapse syn52293417 under ROSMAP controlled access; I did not try them.

a1_downloadable.note: Verified: the processed tables and per-donor PDUI (percentage distal polyA site usage index) matrices download without login from the Broad directory, and the summary statistics are on Zenodo. Raw reads and genotypes are controlled access on Synapse (ROSMAP), but the proposed task does not need them.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Verified: mean PDUI per cell type is a column (Exc, Inh, Ast, Oli, Opc, Mic) for each site. Per-donor values are also columns in the rds matrices.

a3_inputs_present.note: Verified: hg38 coordinates (Loci, Predicted_Proximal_APA) and Ensembl transcript IDs are present, but sequences are not. The sequence comes from one hg38 genome FASTA (a single download, not thousands of lookups).

a4_units_stated.note: PDUI is a unitless fraction; verified in files that it lies in [0, 1] (Exc mean 0.51, SD 0.32). The exact definition comes from DaPars convention, not from the methods text I read.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified: 34,365 unique proximal sites after deduplicating 48,118 rows. Only 4,014 unique sites have values in both Exc and Oli, so cross-cell-type tasks are much smaller.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~25 MB of tables plus ~1 GB for the hg38 genome FASTA
a6_fits_laptop.note: The tables are tiny. The genome FASTA is above the 50 MB cap and has to be fetched by hand, or one chromosome at a time.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Partly consistent: the metadata has 427 donors, the Exc matrix 368 and the abstract says 379. This looks like per-cell-type quality-control filtering of the 427 ROSMAP samples, but I could not confirm it without the methods.

a8_label_provenance.note: The PDUI is estimated from snRNA-seq read coverage by DaPars (a regression on the coverage drop), not predicted from sequence, so it is not circular. Caveat: the proximal site location itself is inferred by DaPars, so the input coordinates and the label come from the same algorithm.

B1.why: One per-site table, but the sequence must be joined from the hg38 genome by coordinates; seen in files.

B2.why: All tsv files parsed first try in pandas; rds matrices read cleanly in R.

B3.why: Same DaPars method in every cell type, but read depth differs widely (Mic has only 1,291 sites).

B4.why: No censored values. Missing values are structural (site not tested in that cell type).

B5.why: 48,118 rows reduce to 34,365 unique sites; transcripts that share a site are duplicated rows.

B6.why: Website summarizes the files; PDUI and column meanings are inferred, not in a data dictionary.

C1.why: Cross-cell-type transfer is informative either way, but the core sequence-to-PDUI task mostly benchmarks.

C2.why: AlphaGenome, Borzoi and Borzoi Prime predict APA (alternative polyadenylation) with open code but were not tested on this cohort.

C3.why: Weak diversity angle: aged prefrontal cortex cell types; Borzoi Prime already trained on a brain atlas.

C4.why: Measuring requires snRNA-seq of hundreds of postmortem brains.

C5.why: Obvious dummies: per-gene mean, PAS (polyadenylation signal) hexamer rule, cell-type mean.

D1.why: RNA-FM and Nucleotide Transformer have open, downloadable weights for 3' UTR sequence.

D2.why: About 34k sequence windows can be embedded once on a CPU with a ridge or GBM head on top.

D3.why: RNA-FM is MIT-licensed; the data is CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo record).

E1.why: Held-out-chromosome split possible; 23 chromosomes present in the site table.

E2.why: 23 chromosomes, each with thousands of sites (chr1 4,317).

E3.why: Per-gene and global mean PDUI computable from the file.

E4.why: Per-donor PDUI matrices (368 donors in Exc) allow a split-half reliability ceiling.

E5.why: Strong AAUAAA/AUUAAA hexamer at the proximal site should mean more proximal usage (lower PDUI).

E6.why: Label shuffle and shuffling within chromosome are straightforward.

E7.why: GTEx-based 3'aQTL-atlas and PolyASite atlas give independent tissue APA data by coordinates.

E8.why: No published ML number on this dataset to reproduce.

G1.why: Ensembl transcript IDs, hg38 coordinates and rsIDs are present in the files.

G2.why: 3'aQTL-atlas (GTEx tissues) and PolyASite 2.0 can be joined on hg38 coordinates and rsID.

G3.why: Transcript-to-site is many-to-one; needs a collapse rule for each site.

G4.why: The join asks whether the cis-code for brain cell-type APA matches bulk tissue; only a modest gain.

H1.why: Full PDUI range for all tested sites, not only significant hits.

H2.why: One cohort (ROSMAP), one brain region, aged donors, 425/427 one race code; seen in metadata.

H4.why: The cohort is described in the paper; the per-cell-type coverage dropout is only visible in the files.

I1.why: Xiong lab (Zhejiang), Boix/Kellis group, and the APA sequence-model community (Calico Borzoi).

I2.why: Could rank 3' UTR variants for follow-up, but only marginally beyond existing models.

I3.why: Spearman correlation on PDUI roughly matches the goal of ranking site usage.

I4.why: The hexamer rule may explain much of it; ML helps for cell-type differences.

J1.why: Real modelling: embeddings, chromosome splits, transfer across cell types.

J2.why: APA biology is moderately intuitive; the hexamer control helps catch errors.

J3.why: Reliability ceiling and hexamer baseline are shareable before any deep model.

J4.why: No budget stated yet; scope fits about 2 weeks.

existing_models.name: AlphaGenome (DeepMind DNA sequence model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported APA Spearman 0.894 vs Borzoi 0.790, and paQTL (polyadenylation QTL) auPRC (area under precision-recall curve) 0.629 within 10 kb of the site, on its own held-out benchmarks from bulk data.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Accuracy on paQTLs decays with distance from the polyA site.

existing_models.name: Borzoi (Calico RNA-seq coverage model)
existing_models.score_and_split: paQTL auPRC 0.621 (as reported in the AlphaGenome comparison).

existing_models.name: Borzoi Prime (bioRxiv 2025, cell-type 3'-seq coverage)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on Tabula Sapiens/Muris and Adult Brain Atlas cell types; scores not retrieved.

existing_models.name: APARENT (Cell 2019, polyA reporter CNN)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on more than 3 million synthetic APA reporters; scores not retrieved.

existing_models.name: DeeReCT-APA (CNN-LSTM site usage model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Mouse tissue site-usage data; scores not retrieved.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (RNA language model) or Nucleotide Transformer on about 500 nt windows around the proximal site

integration.join_key: hg38 coordinates of the proximal polyA site / rsID
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Is the sequence code for brain cell-type APA the same as for bulk tissue APA, or do neurons and glia read 3' UTR sequence differently?

controls.positive_control: Canonical AAUAAA hexamer strength near the proximal site should predict lower PDUI; the per-donor split-half reliability sets the ceiling.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels, and shuffle within chromosome; both should collapse to the per-gene mean baseline.
controls.external_validation: Held-out chromosomes, transfer from Exc to Oli/Inh, and comparison with GTEx 3'aQTL-atlas brain-tissue APA.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts the DaPars-estimated fraction of distal polyA usage in aged prefrontal-cortex cell types of mostly white ROSMAP donors, for sites with enough snRNA-seq 3' coverage, from about 500 nt of genomic sequence.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around a gene's alternative cut-and-tail site to predict how often each brain cell type uses the longer mRNA ending.
plain_idea.train_on: A window of about 500 bases of genome sequence around each of 34,365 candidate shorter-ending sites (verified count), as a numeric summary from a pretrained RNA language model.
plain_idea.predict: The fraction of transcripts using the distal (longer) ending in each of 6 brain cell types. It was measured from single-nucleus RNA sequencing read coverage of 3' UTRs (the untranslated tail of the mRNA) in 368 or more donor brains and estimated by the DaPars algorithm.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tests whether a neuron and a glial cell read the same mRNA-ending sequence signals. That matters for interpreting the paper's 168 disease risk loci that act through mRNA ending choice.

pitch.headline: Open per-donor matrices of mRNA ending choice: 34,387 sites by 368 brains in excitatory neurons, CC-BY data, no login.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Six brain cell types from about 368 aged donors, with per-donor values (0 missing in the Exc matrix), so a measurement-noise ceiling can be computed. The raw reads are controlled access, but these processed tables are open.
pitch.the_win: A frozen RNA language model plus a simple head reaching most of the split-half reliability ceiling on held-out chromosomes, and beating a hexamer-rule baseline in correlation with the measured value.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn how noisy single-nucleus APA estimates are (from the split-half ceiling), and whether cell-type differences can be predicted from sequence at all. Only 4,014 sites are measured in both Exc and Oli.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Xiong (Zhejiang) and Boix/Kellis groups, who could prioritize 3'aQTL variants, and the Calico Borzoi team, who need external cell-type APA tests.

ml_idea: Embed about 500 nt around each proximal site with frozen RNA-FM, then fit a ridge/GBM head to per-cell-type mean PDUI. Use held-out-chromosome CV, cap performance by the per-donor split-half reliability, and test transfer from Exc-trained to Oli/Inh sites.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: about 34k windows at roughly 6-10 per second for RNA-FM on CPU; the tables are 25 MB; the hg38 FASTA is the largest item.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Compute split-half (odd versus even donors) correlation of per-site PDUI from Exc.PDUI_from_Dapars.rds. If it is below about 0.5, the labels are too noisy to model.

verdict_reason: Open, clean per-site and per-donor PDUI tables pass Part A in the files. But strong open APA sequence models exist (AlphaGenome, Borzoi), the cohort is one population, and label noise in snRNA-derived DaPars estimates is unverified.
